resources.string: %1$s plays the rules of `Ludo`, the race game that grew from the ancient Indian game `Pachisi`.
%1$s holds no user data. Your games, scores, and settings stay on this device, and there are no ads, analytics, or tracking.
%1$s is built with the open-source software, fonts, and sounds below, each used under the licence it's listed with.

Welcome to %1$s! You're Red, racing Green. First, getting out of your yard. Tap the die to roll.
Only a **6** brings a pawn out of the yard, so your turn passed. Watch Green.
Green rolled a **6** and came out. A **6** also earns another roll.
A **6**! Tap a pawn in your yard to bring it out onto your start square.
Your **6** earns another roll. Tap the die.
Tap your pawn to move it **4** squares.
Next, captures. Green's pawn is **4** squares ahead of yours. Tap the die.
A **4**! Tap your pawn to land on Green's and send it back to its yard.
Captured! A capture earns another roll. Tap the die.
Tap your pawn to move on. Green can capture you too, but nobody can on a star or a start square.
Next, home. Your pawn in the home column is **2** squares from home. Tap the die.
Exactly **2**! Tap that pawn to bring it home.
Home! That earns another roll too. Tap the die.
Tap your other pawn to move it on.
Last, winning. Three pawns are home, and the last needs exactly **4**. Tap the die.
A **5** is too many: a pawn needs the exact roll home, so your turn passed.
Your turn again. Tap the die.
Exactly **4**! Tap your last pawn to bring it home and win.

Race your four pawns a full lap of the board and into home, in the middle. The first player to bring all four pawns home wins.
Players take turns clockwise, each rolling one die. To decide who goes first, everyone rolls once, and the highest roll starts. Ties roll again.

The classic rules: roll a 6 to leave the yard, and race all four pawns home
Each player has four pawns, waiting in their own coloured yard.
The track runs all the way round the board, and everyone shares it. Each colour joins it at its own start square.
After a full lap, a pawn turns into its own home column and races to home, in the middle of the board.
Roll the die, then move one of your pawns that many squares.
Only a 6 brings a pawn out of the yard, onto its start square.
Roll a 6 and you roll again. So does capturing a pawn, or bringing one home. Roll three 6s in a row and your turn ends.
If none of your pawns can move, your turn passes.
Land on a rival's pawns to send them back to their yard.
Start squares and star squares are safe: nobody can be captured there.
Your own pawns can share a square, and any pawn can pass any other.
Every capture earns you another roll.
A pawn needs the exact roll to reach home.
Bringing a pawn home earns you another roll, unless it was your last.
The first player to bring all four pawns home wins, and everyone else plays on for the places.
With *Stop at first winner* on in Settings, the game ends as soon as one player has every pawn home. Everyone else is placed by how far their pawns have come.
